title: A failing command in a pipeline is ignored: set -eo pipefail

problem.symptom: The deploy script printed 'deployed' and exited 0 although a step failed
problem.description: By default a pipeline's status is the last command's. pipefail propagates failures; -e stops the script.

files.run.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -eo pipefail
false | true
echo "deployed"

files.check.sh:
out=$(bash run.sh 2>&1)
code=$?
if [ "$code" -eq 0 ]; then echo "failure was swallowed"; exit 1; fi
case "$out" in *deployed*) echo "continued after failure"; exit 1 ;; esac
exit 0

limitations.proves: A failure inside a pipeline stops the script with a non-zero status.
limitations.does_not_prove: Behavior of commands inside if/while conditions, where -e does not apply.
